Welcome to my website!

I’m a PhD researcher turned data scientist with 4+ years of experience analyzing high-frequency biometric and behavioral data, including eye-tracking and human motion.

My work focuses on quantitative modeling and prediction of human behavior, with an emphasis on translating messy experimental data into interpretable, decision-relevant models.

Across academic research and applied projects, I’ve developed strengths in experimental design, causal inference, statistical modeling, and rapid model prototyping, primarily using Python. I’m especially interested in problems where careful measurement and statistical thinking matter as much as raw scale.

This site highlights a selection of projects that reflect how I approach data: formulating precise questions, validating assumptions, and building models that are both rigorous and practical.
